nodes.label: Cars Multi-Object Tracking Demo GIF
nodes.description: Animated 480x270, 111-frame result clip advertising the multi-object-tracker library. A ground-level camera beside a racetrack guardrail watches a line of classic convertibles drive past. Every vehicle carries a thin blue axis-aligned bounding box with a small cyan track-label above it and green centroid/keypoint dots inside. Identity boxes persist and shrink smoothly as cars recede up the track, demonstrating tracking continuity rather than per-frame detection quality.
nodes.rationale: Vehicles on a track were chosen for the headline demo because they move fast and monotonically with little mutual occlusion, which showcases the motion model cleanly.

nodes.label: Persistent Track ID Box Overlay Convention
nodes.description: The library's standard visual output contract: for each tracked object draw a coloured rectangle, print a compact identifier label at the top-left corner of that rectangle, and mark the tracked point(s) inside. The same box colour and identifier follow an object across frames, so an identity switch is visible to the eye as a colour/label change.
nodes.rationale: Rendering identity as a stable label rather than only a box is what turns a detector visualisation into a tracker visualisation — it is the only way a viewer can verify association quality from a GIF.
